# dsh-screenshot-tool
Screenshot capture for DeepSeek Harness on Windows. Two entry points share one capture path:
- **`screenshot` tool** — the model calls it, gets the absolute PNG path plus pixel and byte size, a

nd reads the image back with `read_image`.
- **Camera button** — a control in the composer tool row
(next to the attach button). It captures the desktop, shows a preview panel, and offers download, co
py-to-clipboard, and close.
Both go through a `GET /screenshot` route on the Harness web server that streams PNG bytes; the tool
additionally writes a file into the session working directory.
## Requirements

- Windows (uses `System.Windows.Forms` + `System.Drawing` through PowerShell).
- PowerShell: `pwsh`
7 is preferred, `powershell.exe` is the fallback. It looks for `pwsh` on `PATH`, then `C:\Program Fi
les\PowerShell\7\pwsh.exe`, then Windows PowerShell.

utton appears on the next start.
## Usage
Ask the model to take a screenshot, or call the tool directly:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
`path` is optional. Relative paths resolve against the session working directory; the default is `sc
reenshots/shot-<timestamp>.png` there.
The camera button captures straight away and never writes to disk unless you press **Download**.
## What it touches

- Captures the whole virtual desktop (all monitors) via GDI.
- Spawns one PowerShell process per cap
ture; the script is passed inline, and the output path through the `DSH_SHOT_PATH` environment varia

ble.
- The tool writes the PNG to the path you choose; the button keeps the image in memory until do
The tool writes the PNG to the path you choose; the button keeps the image in memory until download.
## Limitations

- Windows only.
- Captures what is on screen, so occluded windows are not visible.
- Large screensho
ts are downscaled by `read_image`, which can make small text hard to read.
